# Home Environment Manager v0.6.0b103 — pinned weather warning details

Built directly on the verified v0.6.0b102 release. All device and PID control,
window/sleep weather policy, command confirmation and recovery behavior remain unchanged.

**Fixed:** The warning source had a proper native headline but the nested
`details` chip collapsed to icon width in the compact two-row dashboard.
Its popover used browser-auto dismissal, causing it to disappear while users
clicked inside or Home Assistant refreshed card states.

- Warning chips now have a guaranteed visible, responsive width and prioritize
  the actual event/headline. Full description remains in tooltip/detail panel.
- Opening a warning creates a **manual, pinned, top-layer panel** with a visible
  close button, Escape support, responsive scrolling and all original native
  attributes (including nested objects, severity and provider timestamps).
- Clicking outside no longer dismisses the details; frequent HA state updates
  cannot detach them. Live native values refresh in place, preserving panel
  scroll and the separate dashboard scroll.
- Raw attribute strings are escaped. The top summary displays provider HTML
  line breaks as readable paragraphs without executing HTML.
- A native entity link remains bound to the exact configured warning source;
  multiple warnings and duplicate friendly names remain independent.
- The regular two-row weather header, existing other tooltip behavior and HEM
  safety rules are unchanged.

Regressions cover narrow and desktop chip width, the pictured DWD-style
Entwarnung headline, all attributes, nested content escaping, outside clicks,
35 consecutive Home Assistant refreshes, scroll retention, keyboard close,
multiple sources and inactive sources, plus the inherited Beta102 suite.
